note: Cross-checked in the wave 7 close-out against CyberChef 11.5.0 (module source read; the module was run on sample inputs for layouts). The input is hex text and the result is text in the layout of the jsrsasign dump CyberChef prints: one element per line, two spaces per level, the type name and then the value (INTEGER hex, BOOLEAN TRUE or FALSE, ObjectIdentifier name (arcs separated by spaces), strings in single quotes, UTCTime and GeneralizedTime without, SEQUENCE {} for an empty sequence, [n] for context tags, OCTETSTRING, encapsulates and BITSTRING, encapsulates with the nested element below), a line feed after every line. Parameters as CyberChef: start is a position in hex characters (even; only the element at start is shown, with what it contains, and the bytes after it are not read) and truncate keeps that many hex characters at each end of a long value, written first..(total Nbytes)..last (the text is unchanged up to that many bytes). Layout was compared by running CyberChef on a certificate, a CSR and the test vectors; the differences that stay: OID names come from Forge's table of standard names (ecdsa-with-SHA256 where jsrsasign says SHA256withECDSA, prime256v1 for P-256); Forge opens an OCTET STRING or BIT STRING (unused bits 0) only when the whole content is exactly one DER element and never guesses at the content of a primitive context tag (jsrsasign shows a 4-byte [7] iPAddress as a nested BOOLEAN); ENUMERATED is decimal (jsrsasign reads the hex digits as decimal, so 0x0a prints as 0); the other universal string types keep their names (jsrsasign prints UNKNOWN(18) for NumericString), application and private classes print as [APPLICATION n] and [PRIVATE n]; a truncate of 0 shows everything (in CyberChef it shows only ..(total Nbytes)..); a value of zero length has no trailing space; malformed data (cut short, indefinite length, nesting over 64 levels, an odd start) is E_COERCE or E_RANGE where CyberChef prints whatever it could read. Text, not a record tree, because the output pane shows trees only 6 levels deep; the record tree is the shared word asn1:parse. Reads BER definite lengths too.

The hex digits of the content bytes of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER (no tag and length) to dotted text: 2a864886f70d010101 is 1.2.840.113549.1.1.1. Arcs of any size (2.25.<UUID>). An empty input, a cut-short or non-minimal sub-identifier, or more than 4,096 bytes is E_COERCE.

Dotted text to the hex of the content bytes (lower case, no separators, no tag and length). At least two arcs, the first 0 to 2, the second below 40 under 0 and 1, digits without leading zeros; anything else is E_COERCE.

The decoded body of each PEM block (RFC 7468) as lower-case hex, one block per line; text outside the blocks is ignored, the label and the RFC 1421 header lines of old encrypted keys are read and dropped. No block, a block that is not closed or is closed by another label, a nested BEGIN or damaged Base64 is E_COERCE (CyberChef returns nothing for text without a block).

Hex to a PEM block with the header parameter (default CERTIFICATE): the BEGIN line, the Base64 in lines of 64 characters, the END line, each ended by a line feed. An empty header, a non-ASCII or multi-line header, or five hyphens in it is E_RANGE; bad hex is E_COERCE.
